identity.title: Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture Alleviates Knee Osteoarthritis via Inhibition of TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB Signaling and Is Associated With Gut Microbiota Alterations.

content.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the chondroprotective effects of Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture (JDJM) in KOA and to determine whether JDJM modulates the TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB axis and is associated with gut microbiota alterations. METHODS: A KOA model was established in New Zealand rabbits using a modified Videman method (n = 36). Animals were assigned to a blank control group (n = 6) or underwent modeling and were then randomized into the model, JDJM low-, medium-, or high-dose, and positive control groups (n = 6/group). Treatments were administered intragastrically for 6 weeks. Cartilage histopathology, evaluated by H&E staining and OARSI scoring, constituted the primary histopathological assessment, with the OARSI score serving as the quantitative primary endpoint. Secondary mechanistic outcomes included serum inflammatory cytokines and TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB-related measures in cartilage tissue, including NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. In vitro, primary rabbit chondrocytes were exposed to IL-1beta-induced inflammatory stimulation to provide supportive mechanistic evidence through assessment of cell viability, apoptosis, inflammatory mediators, and pathway-related molecules. Molecular docking was additionally performed to explore potential interactions between identified JDJM constituents and TLR4/MD-2, MyD88, and NF-kappaB p65. Fecal 16S rRNA sequencing and related gut microbiota analyses were considered exploratory. RESULTS: Compared with the model group, JDJM attenuated cartilage histopathological damage and reduced OARSI scores, while decreasing serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha, and IFN-gamma). In cartilage tissue, JDJM reduced TLR4, MyD88, and NF-kappaB expression and suppressed NF-kappaB p65 nuclear translocation. In vitro, JDJM increased the viability of IL-1beta-stimulated chondrocytes, reduced apoptosis, and decreased the release of inflammatory mediators. Molecular docking revealed distinct docking profiles of JDJM constituents against TLR4/MD-2, MyD88, and NF-kappaB p65. 16S rRNA sequencing indicated a shift in gut microbiota composition in the KOA model. Following JDJM treatment, microbiota composition was modulated, and several bacterial genera showed significant correlations with inflammatory markers and pathway-related molecules. CONCLUSION: JDJM exerted anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective effects in in vivo KOA models and in vitro primary chondrocytes. These effects may be mediated, at least in part, by inhibition of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-kappaB signaling axis. The observed microbiota changes suggest that the gut-joint axis may contribute to the overall effects, although causal relationships require further validation.
